group.status: PB7 neutral vectors; data only; validated without loading either stack
group.note: The handoff consumes a resolution rather than producing one. Four of these vectors are refusals of things the seam deliberately does not implement; refusing them is what keeps discovery, selection, Provider Sets, and mediation outside version 0.1.

properties.statement: Over every vector in this group, a Binding Plan exists exactly when Interconnection completed — a preflight refusal leaves none behind, and a completed handoff always has one — and wherever a plan exists, the provider that answered is the provision the resolution selected.
properties.why: The seam's product is a plan, so 'a plan exists' has to be an invariant over every path rather than an expectation on the successful one. The substitution vector is where a per-vector expectation would not reach: negotiation must refuse before a plan exists, which is exactly the path that could otherwise leave a half-established member behind.

properties.statement: Over every vector in this group, the provider records an effect only for an interaction attempted while the member is released. Summed across the group, the provider's effect count equals the number of post-Release interactions and nothing else contributes to it.
properties.why: The gate is a claim about every stage, not only the one before Release. Retirement closes it again, so a per-vector expectation written against the pre-Release case would not catch a member that reopened after withdrawal. Counting at the provider rather than reading the observation is deliberate: the observation is what the binding says happened, and the effect counter is what did.

properties.statement: Over every vector in this group, the resolution facts — bindingScope, resolvedComponent, requiredProvider, cardinality, exposure, hostEndpoint — answer identically at every stage: before Interconnection, after it, after Release, and after retirement. They are never re-derived from the plan once one exists.
properties.why: The binding scope is the composition's identity for one requirement position and must outlive the plan; a per-vector check reads it at a single moment and cannot see it change. Stating it over the whole lifecycle is what makes 'the scope survives its plan' a checked claim rather than a description.

given: A resolved 1..1 requirement naming the fixture component in one binding scope
An offered provision naming the fixture provider
when: The handoff runs activation preflight and Interconnection
then: One Binding Plan is frozen for that scope
The plan's hostEndpoint is the requirement's and its provider is the selected provision's
The binding scope is carried on the established binding rather than replaced by the planId
No ordinary interaction has occurred

given: A resolved requirement and an offered provision that have passed preflight
when: The member is inspected before Interconnection runs
then: The resolution facts are answerable: bindingScope, component, requiredProvider, cardinality, exposure, hostEndpoint
No Binding Plan fact is answerable, because no contract has been negotiated
A plan fact answerable here would claim an agreement that does not exist

given: A resolved requirement naming one Component contract
when: The offered provision names a different Component contract
then: The handoff refuses before any conversation exists
No frame is emitted and no provider is started
The refusal is a contract refusal rather than an authority denial

given: A resolved requirement naming a required provider, as a provider-specific resolution does
when: The offered provision names a different provider
then: The handoff refuses rather than accepting a compatible substitute
Selecting among compatible providers is resolution work this seam does not perform

given: A resolved requirement declaring a cardinality other than 1..1
then: The requirement is refused rather than narrowed to its first member
A Provider Set needs membership, exposure, and failure semantics this seam does not own

given: A resolved requirement declaring mediated exposure
then: The requirement is refused rather than erased into a direct binding
An erased Mediation still carries provenance, deputy, and authority obligations, so erasing one silently would be the defect

given: A resolution that selected one provider
An endpoint that offers the required Component contract but answers as a different provider
then: Contract negotiation refuses the provider mismatch as Decision 11 requires
No Binding Plan is produced, because the answering provider is not the one the required contract names
The handoff's composition check remains a second fail-closed boundary for a resolution that selected a different provision
The binding is not released and no ordinary interaction occurs

given: An established binding whose provider has signalled readiness
The ordinary-interaction gate has not been released
then: The interaction is refused as a state violation
No frame is emitted and the provider records no effect
Establishment, readiness, withdrawal, and termination remain permitted, because they are lifecycle traffic rather than ordinary interaction

given: A member whose Interconnection did not complete, so no readiness signal arrived
when: Release is attempted for that member
then: Release is refused as a state violation
The gate stays closed, so no ordinary interaction can follow a release that did not happen

given: An established and ready binding in one binding scope
when: The composition releases it and an ordinary interaction runs
then: The interaction reaches the provider and produces a successful Outcome
The observation reports the same plan the handoff froze

given: A released binding in one binding scope
when: The composition withdraws and terminates it
then: A replacement record names the scope, the retired plan, the component, the provider that answered, and the terminal state
The gate is closed again, so no ordinary interaction follows withdrawal
Re-establishing the same scope produces a new planId, because there is no renegotiation in place
The record grants nothing: the replacement resolves, preflights, negotiates, and releases from the beginning
